source: PubMed Central open-access case reports 2024-2026, screened in data/layer_a_raw/screening_final.csv

cases.title: From 60% to 5% in 12 Weeks: A Trastuzumab-Induced Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Drop
cases.decision_point: Emergency visit one week after the first maintenance trastuzumab dose
cases.record_text:
54-year-old woman. History: acute promyelocytic leukaemia 2012-2015 treated with tretinoin, idarubicin, mitoxantrone and mercaptopurine; LVEF normal (>55%) on four echocardiograms 2012-2017.
2022: stage IA invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast, ER+, PR-, HER2 3+; lumpectomy.
Day 0 (June 2022): started weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 + trastuzumab 2 mg/kg for 12 weeks, then radiotherapy. Baseline echo day 0: LVEF 55-60%, normal diastolic function, GLS -14%.
Day 90 (September): echo LVEF 60-65%, moderately dilated left atrium.
Day 174 (November): first maintenance dose of trastuzumab 6 mg/kg (planned 9 months).
Day 181 (today, emergency department): one day of progressive dyspnoea, orthopnoea and bilateral leg swelling. Bibasal crackles, 2+ pitting oedema. ECG sinus tachycardia, low-voltage QRS. Troponin I negative. NT-proBNP 2035 pg/mL. Chest X-ray: pulmonary vascular congestion. Echo: severe diffuse LV hypokinesis, moderately dilated LV, LVEF 5%. Admitted; intravenous furosemide given.
No blood count or temperature reported.
cases.practice: Trastuzumab discontinued; GDMT (sacubitril/valsartan, metoprolol, dapagliflozin, later spironolactone); LVEF 10% at 2 months, 33% at 7 months; referred to advanced HF clinic.

key_overrides.reason: Emergency admission (acute heart failure / stroke with LV thrombus): level 1 is appropriate, not over-triage.

review_notes: LVEF 5% is below the tools' plausibility limit (15%), so the tools ask for the echo to be verified (defer). Holding treatment is accepted as correct either way. Decide whether this case should instead be keyed as a confirmed severe CTRCD.

cases.title: A cycle of complications: trastuzumab-induced takotsubo cardiomyopathy causing LV thrombus
cases.decision_point: Admission for ischaemic stroke; echo shows reduced LVEF with LV thrombus
cases.record_text:
77-year-old woman, well-controlled hypertension, stage IV breast cancer diagnosed 2019, currently on trastuzumab and capecitabine.
Today: admitted with right-sided weakness, facial droop and slurred speech (NIHSS 9); MRI: acute left frontal ischaemic stroke.
Vitals: BP 156/75 mmHg, pulse 62/min, temperature 97.8 F (36.6 C), SpO2 96%. Lungs clear, no oedema.
Labs: haemoglobin 12.3 g/dL, WBC 6.1 x10^3/uL (differential not reported), platelets 238 x10^3/uL; creatinine 1.2 mg/dL (ref 0.5-1.0), eGFR 48; troponin 0.02 ng/mL (ref 0-0.033); bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL (ref 0.2-1.3); ALT 23 U/L (ref 0-34); AST 51 U/L (ref 14-36).
Echo: LVEF 35%, wall-motion abnormalities of the distal septum, apex and distal walls suggestive of takotsubo; 0.9 x 1 cm LV thrombus; grade I diastolic dysfunction.
No baseline (pre-trastuzumab) echo is available in the record. She had a previous episode of reduced LVEF on trastuzumab that resolved after it was stopped.
cases.practice: Anticoagulation; losartan + carvedilol; trastuzumab and capecitabine held; LVEF 60% two weeks after discharge; trastuzumab held indefinitely, capecitabine resumed.

key_overrides.reason: Emergency admission (acute heart failure / stroke with LV thrombus): level 1 is appropriate, not over-triage.

review_notes: No baseline LVEF in the record: the specification asks for it (defer/hold). A clinician would hold trastuzumab regardless; holding is accepted.

cases.title: Irreversible cardiotoxicity induced by trastuzumab: a pharmacovigilance case report
cases.decision_point: One week after the 13th weekly trastuzumab dose: new dyspnoea and LVEF 37%
cases.record_text:
61-year-old woman; hypertension (losartan), type 2 diabetes (metformin), hypothyroidism, obesity.
Stage 3 HER2+ breast cancer (ER-, PR-), breast-conserving surgery.
Doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2, 4 cycles every 3 weeks (cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2). LVEF 68% before chemotherapy, 56% after the 4 cycles.
Day 0: started weekly paclitaxel + trastuzumab (4 mg/kg loading, then 2 mg/kg weekly).
Day 77 (5 minutes after the 12th trastuzumab infusion): acute dyspnoea, HR 130, BP 160/102, SpO2 90%; CT: interstitial pneumonitis; NT-proBNP 1750 pg/mL, LDH 546 U/L, AST 546 U/L, ALT 502 U/L, ALP 345 U/L, glucose 386 mg/dL; treated for community-acquired pneumonia (normal WBC) with piperacillin/tazobactam.
Day 84: 13th trastuzumab dose given, radiotherapy started.
Day 91 (today): shortness of breath again. ECG: new left bundle branch block. Echo: LVEF 37%.
No current blood count, liver tests or temperature reported.
cases.practice: Bisoprolol + spironolactone started; LVEF 35% two weeks later and trastuzumab discontinued; LVEF 29% at 2 months, remained reduced to 2023.
review_notes: Symptomatic heart failure severity is not graded (HF status left undocumented); the key uses the asymptomatic ESC category from LVEF (56% to 37%: severe).

cases.title: Breast cancer surgery under mechanical circulatory support in a patient with CTRCD
cases.decision_point: Admission with decompensated heart failure after 3 cycles of trastuzumab/pertuzumab/paclitaxel
cases.record_text:
40-year-old woman, stage II invasive carcinoma of the right breast, hormone receptor positive, HER2 overexpressing, high proliferation.
Baseline echo: LVEF 58%, GLS -18%.
Epirubicin + cyclophosphamide, 4 cycles (cumulative epirubicin 360 mg/m2).
Day 70: echo LVEF 52%, GLS -16% (subclinical dysfunction); carvedilol started; up-titration not possible because of hypotension.
Then trastuzumab + pertuzumab + paclitaxel, 3 cycles.
Day 147 (today): symptomatic decompensated heart failure; echo LVEF 25%; hospital admission.
No laboratory values or temperature reported.
cases.practice: Inotropes; circulatory collapse day 17 of admission; Impella + PCPS; breast surgery under Impella; LVEF recovered to 40%; anti-HER2 therapy not resumed in the report.

key_overrides.reason: Emergency admission (acute heart failure / stroke with LV thrombus): level 1 is appropriate, not over-triage.

cases.title: Takotsubo Syndrome during Pertuzumab and Trastuzumab Therapy for HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer
cases.decision_point: Hospitalisation for chest pain on maintenance pertuzumab/trastuzumab; LVEF 47%
cases.record_text:
57-year-old woman; hypertension (ramipril), hypercholesterolaemia (atorvastatin); ECOG 0.
2017: HER2+ breast cancer pT2 pN1 treated with surgery, epirubicin + cyclophosphamide + docetaxel, trastuzumab and letrozole.
May 2022: bone metastases. Day 0 (June 2022): paclitaxel + pertuzumab + trastuzumab, then from October maintenance pertuzumab + trastuzumab + fulvestrant + denosumab (complete metabolic response).
Day 300 (today, March 2023): emergency admission with typical chest pain radiating to the left arm (50 min), a similar episode 2 days earlier. ECG: diffuse negative T waves, QTc 486 ms. Cardiac biomarkers increased (values not reported). Coronary angiography: no obstructive lesions; ventriculography: mid-apical hypokinesia, basal hyperkinesia (takotsubo pattern). Echo: LVEF 47%, apical hypokinesia. Haemodynamically stable.
No baseline echo before the current anti-HER2 course, no laboratory values and no temperature reported.
cases.practice: Discharged on aspirin + bisoprolol; pertuzumab/trastuzumab not given (fulvestrant + denosumab only); LVEF 52% in July 2023, anti-HER2 resumed after CA15-3 rise; LVEF 55% in August.
review_notes: No baseline LVEF: LVEF 47% cannot be judged as a fall, so the key asks for the baseline (defer); holding anti-HER2 is accepted.

cases.title: Reversible Heart Failure After Anthracycline and Alkylating Agent Chemotherapy
cases.decision_point: Echo one month after completing dose-dense AC + paclitaxel, before adjuvant radiotherapy
cases.record_text:
41-year-old woman, current smoker (4-5 cigarettes/day), otherwise healthy.
Early right breast cancer (invasive carcinoma NST + DCIS), ER+, PR+, HER2-negative; no metastases. Mastectomy with flap reconstruction June 2024; troponin and NT-proBNP normal before treatment.
Baseline echo: LVEF 64%, structurally normal.
Day 0 (July 2024): dose-dense doxorubicin + cyclophosphamide, then paclitaxel; completed November 2024. Intermittent chest pain, dyspnoea and dry cough during chemotherapy; coronary CT angiography normal (calcium score 0).
Day 150 (today, December 2024): echo: mildly dilated LV, LVEF 40-45%, multiple regional wall-motion abnormalities, GLS -16.9%. Holter: no arrhythmia. Adjuvant radiotherapy is planned.
No current laboratory values or temperature reported.
cases.practice: Diagnosed chemotherapy-induced cardiomyopathy; GDMT (ramipril, dapagliflozin, spironolactone, bisoprolol); LVEF 50-55% after 6 weeks; radiotherapy completed; normal LVEF later.
review_notes: Anthracycline already completed: 'hold' refers to further cardiotoxic therapy. The key requires heart-failure therapy (moderate CTRCD, ESC 2022).

cases.title: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Carrier and Breast Cancer Treatment-Related Cardiomyopathy
cases.decision_point: Surveillance echo after 3 months of TCHP: LVEF fall from 63.8% to 55.8%
cases.record_text:
Woman in her mid-thirties; thyroid nodule, lipomas. cT2N1M0 grade 3 invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR+, HER2 amplified. Recently confirmed carrier of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (dystrophin exon 45-50 deletion).
Baseline echo: LVEF 63.8%, GLS -16.73%.
Day 0: neoadjuvant carboplatin, docetaxel, trastuzumab and pertuzumab (6 cycles planned), then adjuvant trastuzumab + pertuzumab. One hospitalisation for neutropenic fever (viral URTI) during the course, resolved.
Day 90 (today): asymptomatic. Surveillance echo LVEF 55.76%, GLS could not be measured. High-sensitivity troponin and BNP normal (BNP 21 pg/mL). AST 52 U/L, ALT 55 U/L (creatine kinase not checked).
No current blood count or temperature reported.
cases.practice: Cardiology referral, carvedilol 3.125 mg twice daily; LVEF 55% and GLS -17.46% one month later; anti-HER2 therapy completed without interruption; LVEF 64% after 2 years.

cases.title: Treatment with Phesgo in a patient receiving hemodialysis
cases.decision_point: Surveillance echo after 5 months of subcutaneous pertuzumab/trastuzumab on haemodialysis
cases.record_text:
Woman diagnosed 2019 (age 52 then) with cT3N3M0 ER+ HER2 3+ breast cancer; end-stage kidney disease on haemodialysis 3 times a week since 1998 (Fanconi syndrome, failed transplant); secondary hypertension, severe pulmonary hypertension, chronic hepatitis C. Refused chemotherapy.
2020-2022: subcutaneous trastuzumab + tamoxifen (no cardiac toxicity); progression July 2022.
Echo May 2022: LVEF 53%, GLS -15.8%.
Day 0 (August 2022): Phesgo (subcutaneous pertuzumab + trastuzumab) every 21 days, given between dialysis sessions, + exemestane. Good response.
Echo September 2022: LVEF 50%, GLS -15.7%.
Day 150 (today, January 2023): echo LVEF 50% (GLS not measured). Asymptomatic.
No laboratory values or temperature reported.
cases.practice: Phesgo continued to 10 cycles; LVEF 53% (GLS -16.3%) in April 2023; stopped for progression.

cases.title: Long-term control of brain metastases with over 100 cycles of T-DM1
cases.decision_point: Routine echo during long-term T-DM1: LVEF 53% (67% in 2016)
cases.record_text:
Woman, HER2+ invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast diagnosed 2015 at age 39 (ER-, PR-).
Neoadjuvant docetaxel + doxorubicin, mastectomy 2016 (pT3N1a), radiotherapy and adjuvant trastuzumab. Echo January 2016: LVEF 67%.
2018: lung and bone metastases; docetaxel + trastuzumab + pertuzumab, progression; denosumab.
2019: brain metastases (craniotomy, radiosurgery to 7 lesions).
Day 0 (May 2019): T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg every 3 weeks, disease stable since.
Day 1000 (today, February 2022): routine echo LVEF 53%. No heart-failure symptoms. ECOG 1.
No GLS, cardiac biomarkers, laboratory values or temperature reported.
cases.practice: Judged not to meet criteria for interruption; T-DM1 continued with 3-4-monthly echo; 107 cycles in total; LVEF 59% in December 2025.
review_notes: A 'continue with monitoring' case: LVEF fell 14 points but stayed >= 50%.

cases.title: Antitumor therapy and cardiovascular safety management in a breast cancer patient with coronary disease
cases.decision_point: Echo after 6 cycles of docetaxel/trastuzumab/pertuzumab, before continuing anti-HER2
cases.record_text:
62-year-old woman; hypertension, diabetes, coronary heart disease with LAD stent (2019); on valsartan, metformin, clopidogrel, rosuvastatin.
Grade II invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast with axillary node metastasis, ER/PR negative, HER2 overexpressing. Baseline: normal liver/kidney function, BNP and troponin normal; echo LVEF 69%.
High cardiovascular risk, so anthracyclines were avoided. Day 0: docetaxel + trastuzumab + pertuzumab every 3 weeks, 6 cycles; LVEF checked every 3 months.
Day 126 (today): echo LVEF 59%. No cardiovascular symptoms.
No GLS or current laboratory values reported.
cases.practice: Mastectomy (no residual invasive cancer), radiotherapy with heart-dose limits; no cardiovascular complications reported.
review_notes: Optional case; timing of the 59% echo is approximate in the report.

cases.title: Febrile neutropenia caused by the rare organism Phytobacter
cases.decision_point: Hospital arrival on day 12 of cycle 3 with fever
cases.record_text:
62-year-old woman, HER2+ carcinoma of the right breast cT4bN2M0, on neoadjuvant trastuzumab (8 mg/kg loading, then 6 mg/kg), carboplatin AUC 6 and docetaxel 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks.
Today = day 12 of cycle 3: presents with fever, headache and severe fatigue. Conscious, febrile (temperature value not recorded), pulse 110/min, BP 130/70 mmHg, severe pallor, retinal haemorrhages.
Labs: haemoglobin 3.7 g/dL, total leucocytes 1.05 x10^9/L, ANC 0.294 x10^9/L, platelets 5 x10^9/L; lactate and biochemistry normal; chest X-ray normal.
cases.practice: Blood/urine cultures, piperacillin-tazobactam + teicoplanin, filgrastim, red-cell and platelet transfusion; Phytobacter bacteraemia; recovered day 7; later cycles with reduced-dose taxane.

key_overrides.reason: Fever is documented in words ('febrile') without a number, so the tools cannot grade febrile neutropenia; clinically this is febrile neutropenia (ESMO 2016/CTCAE v6.0 grade 3).

review_notes: Key corrected by hand: documented fever without a value.

cases.title: Management of sepsis complicated by eroded mixed hemorrhoids following breast cancer chemotherapy
cases.decision_point: Admission 7 days after cycle 1 of TCHP with 2 days of fever
cases.record_text:
51-year-old woman, invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast cT2N1M0, ER-, PR-, HER2+.
Day 0: cycle 1 of neoadjuvant TCHP (docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab, pertuzumab); no prophylactic G-CSF.
Day 7 (today): admitted with 2 days of fever, highest temperature 40.1 C. Constipation with manual evacuation; prolapsed mixed haemorrhoids, tender dark-purple fluctuant perianal mass with exudate.
Labs: WBC 0.17 x10^9/L (differential/ANC not reported), platelets 6 x10^9/L, RBC 2.55 x10^12/L.
cases.practice: Meropenem (vancomycin day 5, amikacin + amphotericin B day 10), parenteral nutrition, leukocyte/platelet support, local wound care; E. coli bacteraemia; afebrile after 30 days.

key_overrides.reason: Fever 40.1 C with WBC 170/uL: ANC is not reported but cannot be >= 500/uL; empirical antibiotics and cultures are required now, not after the ANC is known (ESMO 2016).

review_notes: Tests the missing-ANC rule: the answer must treat this as febrile neutropenia.

cases.title: Preventing chemotherapy-induced neutropenia with different timings of PEG-G-CSF (case 1)
cases.decision_point: Routine day-8 blood count after cycle 1 of FEC100
cases.record_text:
55-year-old woman, stage IIA invasive ductal carcinoma (pT1cN1mi), ER+, PR+, HER2 3+; partial mastectomy. ECOG 0, BSA 1.39 m2.
Pre-treatment labs: WBC 4930/mm3, neutrophils 2830/mm3, platelets 202,000/mm3, bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL, ALT 16, AST 14 U/L, creatinine 0.57 mg/dL.
Day 0: cycle 1 of adjuvant FEC100 (5-FU 470, epirubicin 94, cyclophosphamide 470 mg/m2); pegfilgrastim on day 3. Mild fatigue and anorexia, resolved with antiemetics.
Day 8 (today, routine check): WBC 1050/mm3, neutrophils 170/mm3. No fever reported (temperature value not recorded).
cases.practice: Prophylactic levofloxacin for 3 days; counts recovered next day without G-CSF; next cycles with 8% dose reduction and pegfilgrastim moved to day 4.

key_overrides.reason: The report states the patient had no fever; the value is simply not given. Afebrile grade 3-4 neutropenia at the day-8 nadir: closer monitoring (level 3) or modifying the next cycle (level 2) are both accepted.

review_notes: Text gives neutrophils 170/mm3, the summary table 190/mm3; 170 used.

cases.title: Preventing chemotherapy-induced neutropenia with different timings of PEG-G-CSF (case 2)
cases.decision_point: Routine day-8 blood count after cycle 1 of dose-dense EC
cases.record_text:
41-year-old woman, stage IIB invasive ductal carcinoma (pT2N1M0), ER+, PR+, HER2 0; partial mastectomy planned after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. ECOG 0, BSA 1.42 m2.
Pre-treatment labs: WBC 7070/mm3, neutrophils 4770/mm3, platelets 202,000/mm3, bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, ALT 20, AST 11 U/L, creatinine 0.5 mg/dL.
Day 0: cycle 1 of dose-dense epirubicin 85 mg/m2 + cyclophosphamide 560 mg/m2; pegfilgrastim on day 3. Mild fatigue and anorexia.
Day 8 (today, outpatient routine check): WBC 520/mm3, neutrophils 20/mm3. No fever and no symptoms reported (temperature value not recorded).
cases.practice: Urgent admission, G-CSF + meropenem then levofloxacin, air purifier; counts rose next day; cycle 2 dose reduced 16-18% with pegfilgrastim on day 4.

key_overrides.reason: The report states the patient had no fever; the value is simply not given. Afebrile grade 3-4 neutropenia at the day-8 nadir: closer monitoring (level 3) or modifying the next cycle (level 2) are both accepted.

cases.title: Preventing chemotherapy-induced neutropenia with different timings of PEG-G-CSF (case 3)
cases.decision_point: Routine day-8 blood count after cycle 1 of dose-dense EC
cases.record_text:
62-year-old woman, stage I invasive ductal carcinoma (pT1N0M0), ER-, PgR-, HER2 1+, Ki67 72%; partial mastectomy. ECOG 0, BSA 1.58 m2.
Pre-treatment labs: WBC 5000/mm3, neutrophils 2990/mm3, platelets 194,000/mm3, bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, ALT 20, AST 11 U/L, creatinine 0.56 mg/dL.
Day 0: cycle 1 of adjuvant dose-dense epirubicin 89 mg/m2 + cyclophosphamide 560 mg/m2; pegfilgrastim on day 3. Mild nausea.
Day 8 (today, routine check): WBC 600/mm3, neutrophils 90/mm3, platelets 58,000/mm3. No fever reported (temperature value not recorded).
cases.practice: G-CSF for 3 days + oral levofloxacin; cycle 2 at ~90% dose with pegfilgrastim on day 4.

key_overrides.reason: The report states the patient had no fever; the value is simply not given. Afebrile grade 3-4 neutropenia at the day-8 nadir: closer monitoring (level 3) or modifying the next cycle (level 2) are both accepted.

cases.title: Preventing chemotherapy-induced neutropenia with different timings of PEG-G-CSF (case 4)
cases.decision_point: Routine day-8 blood count after cycle 1 of EC
cases.record_text:
72-year-old woman, stage IIA invasive lobular carcinoma (pT2N0M0), ER+, PgR-, HER2 2+ (FISH negative); total mastectomy. ECOG 0, BSA 1.41 m2.
Pre-treatment labs: WBC 8000/mm3, neutrophils 5260/mm3, platelets 359,000/mm3, bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL, ALT 20, AST 24 U/L, creatinine 0.68 mg/dL.
Day 0: cycle 1 of adjuvant epirubicin 85 mg/m2 + cyclophosphamide 567 mg/m2; pegfilgrastim on day 3. Mild constipation only.
Day 8 (today, outpatient routine check): WBC 1100/mm3, neutrophils 140/mm3. No fever reported (temperature value not recorded).
cases.practice: Oral levofloxacin; pharyngitis with 37.6 C on day 19 (neutrophils 7900); cycle 2 at 87% dose with pegfilgrastim on day 4.

key_overrides.reason: The report states the patient had no fever; the value is simply not given. Afebrile grade 3-4 neutropenia at the day-8 nadir: closer monitoring (level 3) or modifying the next cycle (level 2) are both accepted.

cases.title: G-CSF-induced aortitis in an elderly woman managed with prednisolone
cases.decision_point: Admission on day 13 of EC cycle 1 with persistent fever >= 39 C
cases.record_text:
72-year-old woman, stage IIB triple-negative invasive ductal carcinoma (T2N1M0); mastectomy + axillary dissection. Planned adjuvant EC x4 then weekly paclitaxel x12.
Day 0: cycle 1 of epirubicin + cyclophosphamide (pre-dose WBC 3150/uL, neutrophils 2053/uL, platelets 294,000/uL, albumin 4.1 g/dL, CRP 0.101 mg/dL); pegfilgrastim on day 2 (on-body injector).
From day 9: persistent fever >= 39.0 C.
Day 13 (today, admission): conscious, physically well, no focal signs of infection. WBC 18,240/uL, neutrophils 15,887/uL, platelets 328,000/uL, albumin 2.5 g/dL, CRP 28.0 mg/dL. Influenza and COVID-19 antigens negative; non-contrast CT shows no source.
cases.practice: Cultures + sulbactam/ampicillin; day 15 contrast CT: aortitis; prednisolone 60 mg; fever resolved; EC not resumed.

key_overrides.reason: Fever >= 39 C with a high CRP needs an infection work-up (level 3 or more urgent), even without neutropenia.

review_notes: Fever without neutropenia: tests that an answer does not label this febrile neutropenia; infection work-up and delaying the next cycle are accepted.

cases.title: G-CSF-induced aortitis: a case report
cases.decision_point: Hospital visit on day 17 of EC cycle 1 with recurrent fever 39 C
cases.record_text:
67-year-old woman, ER+ HER2+ breast cancer; hepatitis B carrier, mitral regurgitation, glaucoma.
Day 0: primary systemic chemotherapy, EC (epirubicin 90 mg/m2 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2) with dexamethasone days 1-4; pegylated G-CSF 3.6 mg on day 4.
Day 11: fever up to 38 C; levofloxacin started as for febrile neutropenia (no blood count reported).
Day 17 (today): fever 39 C again; examination otherwise normal. WBC 33,800/uL (neutrophils 91.8%, about 31,000/uL), CRP 19.6 mg/dL, ESR 123 mm/h, D-dimer 3.3 ug/mL; COVID-19 PCR negative.
cases.practice: CT: aortic wall thickening (aortitis); cultures negative; no steroids; fever resolved by day 30; EC resumed at reduced dose.

key_overrides.reason: Fever >= 39 C with a high CRP needs an infection work-up (level 3 or more urgent), even without neutropenia.

review_notes: Fever without neutropenia (high neutrophils after pegfilgrastim).

cases.title: Trastuzumab Emtansine (T-DM1)-Induced Porto-Sinusoidal Vascular Disorder
cases.decision_point: Liver tests before a T-DM1 dose after 13 months: bilirubin rising to 1.9 mg/dL
cases.record_text:
Woman, grade 3 HER2 3+ ER/PR-negative breast carcinoma diagnosed 7 years ago at age 43: neoadjuvant doxorubicin + cyclophosphamide x4, docetaxel + trastuzumab x4, lumpectomy (ypTis N0), radiotherapy, 1 year of trastuzumab.
Recurrence 3.5 years later (pectoral muscle, lung, hilar nodes; no liver metastases). ECOG 0.
Day 0 (February 2021): T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg every 3 weeks. Before T-DM1: bilirubin 0.4 mg/dL, AST 13 U/L, platelets 360,000/uL. Complete radiological response at 6 months.
Since the first cycle: persistent grade 1 rise of transaminases and GGT. From month 9: bilirubin above normal and mild thrombocytopenia.
Day 395 (today, March 2022, before the next dose): total bilirubin 1.9 mg/dL (ref 0.2-1.2), AST 55 U/L (ref 5-34), ALT 50 U/L (ref <55), GGT 76 U/L, ALP 199 U/L, platelets 170,000/uL. Asymptomatic, no new medicines.
No blood count differential, temperature or echo reported.
cases.practice: T-DM1 continued; dose reduced to 3 mg/kg in June 2022 and 2.4 mg/kg in August 2022 for grade 2 hyperbilirubinaemia; porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder diagnosed; T-DM1 stopped after 22 months.

key_overrides.reason: Blood count and temperature are not reported and are not needed for this liver decision. T-DM1 label: grade 2 hyperbilirubinaemia means withhold until grade <= 1, then resume (dose reduction if recurrent); holding or reducing are both accepted, so a dose reduction is not required.

review_notes: The hepatic dose bands in the specification are the doxorubicin label's; for T-DM1 the requirement 'dose reduction' is kept but 'hold' is also accepted.

cases.title: Drug-Induced Sclerosing Cholangitis Leading to Discontinuation of Treatment
cases.decision_point: Day 49 after the first T-DXd dose: jaundice, bilirubin 5.0 mg/dL
cases.record_text:
Woman, right breast cancer with vertebral metastasis diagnosed 2014 at age 48 (ER+, PR+, HER2 2+, FISH negative). Endocrine therapy, then fulvestrant + palbociclib, then paclitaxel + bevacizumab (stopped for neuropathy). No previous liver toxicity. Performance status 1.
Day 0 (2024): first dose of trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd). Liver tests normal before it.
Day 17: fatigue; GGT 373 U/L, CRP 19 mg/dL, transaminases normal; E. coli bacteraemia; CT: intrahepatic bile-duct dilatation without obstruction; treated with antibiotics, discharged day 32.
Day 49 (today): jaundice; liver palpable 1 cm. Total bilirubin 5.0 mg/dL (ref 0.4-1.5), GGT 839 U/L, CRP 15 mg/dL; transaminases within normal limits (values not given); blood cultures again E. coli; CT: strictures and dilatations of the intrahepatic bile ducts.
No blood count, temperature or echo reported.
cases.practice: ERCP with biliary drain; biopsy: drug-induced cholangitis; further chemotherapy judged unfeasible; best supportive care; died day 99.

hold_reasons: grade 3 hyperbilirubinaemia (> 3 x ULN) on T-DXd with cholangitis (label: withhold)
key_overrides.reason: The specification's bilirubin hold rule is the doxorubicin label (> 5 mg/dL); for T-DXd a bilirubin > 3 x ULN requires withholding.

review_notes: Key corrected by hand: T-DXd label instead of doxorubicin label.

cases.title: Trastuzumab deruxtecan in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer with severe hepatic dysfunction
cases.decision_point: Before starting second-line T-DXd with progressing liver metastases and hepatic dysfunction
cases.record_text:
Woman, multicentric grade 3 invasive breast carcinoma diagnosed May 2020 at age 40 (then HER2 1+): mastectomy pT3N1mi, adjuvant doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide then docetaxel, chest-wall radiotherapy, ovarian suppression + exemestane.
July 2023: bone, liver and nodal metastases; biopsy now ER 90%, HER2 amplified. Pertuzumab + trastuzumab + docetaxel, then maintenance dual anti-HER2 + endocrine therapy; stable until June 2024.
Today (August 2024): progression of liver metastases; second-line trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is being considered. Labs: total bilirubin 5.9 mg/dL (ref 0.3-1.2), AST 130 U/L (<35), ALT 142 U/L (<35), GGT 1373 U/L. ECOG 1, grade 1 fatigue only, not icteric; ultrasound: no biliary obstruction.
No blood count, temperature or echo reported.
cases.practice: MDT started T-DXd at the lowest dose (3.2 mg/kg) with steroids and close monitoring; liver tests normalised in 3 weeks; dose escalated to 5.4 mg/kg; partial response, PFS ~12 months.

key_overrides.reason: Liver dysfunction is caused by the tumour the drug is meant to treat; guidelines give no rule. Withholding (deferring) or starting at a reduced dose with close monitoring are both acceptable; full-dose treatment without a dose adjustment is not.

review_notes: Judgement case: please confirm the accepted answers with the clinician.

cases.title: Severe thrombocytopaenia caused by trastuzumab emtansine in a patient with breast cancer
cases.decision_point: Admission on day 5 after the first adjuvant T-DM1 dose
cases.record_text:
48-year-old woman, HER2+ early left breast cancer. Neoadjuvant epirubicin 90 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 x4, then pertuzumab + trastuzumab + docetaxel x4; partial mastectomy: residual 15 mm invasive ductal carcinoma (ER-, PR-, HER2+), sentinel node negative.
Day 0: first dose of adjuvant T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg (14 planned). Before it: platelets 59,000/uL, AST 21, ALT 13 U/L, bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL. Also taking tamoxifen, rabeprazole, furosemide.
Day 2: grade 2 rash, subcutaneous bleeding at the knee.
Day 5 (today, admission): platelets 18,000/uL, AST 254 U/L, ALT 193 U/L, total bilirubin 1.3 mg/dL.
No reference ranges, blood count differential, temperature or echo reported.
cases.practice: Tamoxifen stopped; glycyrrhizin; platelet transfusions; recovery by day 7 (platelets 59,000, AST/ALT 89/88).

hold_reasons: grade 3 transaminase elevation and grade 4 thrombocytopenia on T-DM1 (label: withhold)
key_overrides.reason: The specification has no rule for T-DM1 hepatotoxicity or platelets; T-DM1 label: withhold for AST/ALT > 5 x ULN or platelets < 25,000/uL.

review_notes: Key corrected by hand (T-DM1 label). Reference ranges not reported: defaults used.

cases.title: Severe Inflammatory Cystitis and Ureteritis Following Neoadjuvant TCHP
cases.decision_point: Emergency visit after cycle 1 of TCHP with haematuria and acute kidney injury
cases.record_text:
65-year-old woman, HER2-positive hormone-receptor-negative T2N1 left breast cancer, no other history.
Day 0: cycle 1 of neoadjuvant TCHP (docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab, pertuzumab).
Day 10 (today, emergency department): abdominal pain and visible haematuria; haemodynamically stable. Creatinine 98 umol/L (1.11 mg/dL) from baseline 62 umol/L (0.70 mg/dL); eGFR 52 from > 90 mL/min/1.73m2; haemoglobin 130 g/L. Urine: haematuria and pyuria, culture negative. No coagulopathy or thrombocytopenia. Ultrasound: bilateral hydronephrosis; CT: bilateral hydroureter with peri-ureteric inflammation, no stones.
No blood count differential, temperature or echo reported.
cases.practice: IV fluids, bladder irrigation, fosfomycin; creatinine rose to 129 umol/L; prednisolone 60 mg with fast recovery; MDT stopped neoadjuvant chemotherapy and went to surgery.

key_overrides.reason: Decision is about kidney injury on a regimen with renally dosed carboplatin; blood count/temperature are not needed to decide (patient not febrile in the report). AKI (KDIGO stage 1) needs at least level 3; holding the next cycle (level 2) is accepted.

review_notes: Carboplatin is dosed by renal function: holding the next cycle is accepted.
